The AF3 output contract the finding relies on is real: I fetched google-deepmind/alphafold3 docs/output.md this session and it lists exactly `<job_name>_model.cif`, `_confidences.json`, `_summary_confidences.json`, `_data.json`, `ranking_scores.csv`, with array fields `pae, atom_plddts, contact_probs, token_chain_ids, atom_chain_ids` and summary fields `ptm, iptm, fraction_disordered, has_clash, ranking_score, chain_pair_pae_min, chain_pair_iptm, chain_ptm, chain_iptm, chain_ids`, ranking_score range "[-100, 1.5]", pLDDT "a per-atom confidence estimate on a 0-100 scale". So the finding stands. Two factual errors in the write-up must be fixed before issue. Correction: (1) The parenthetical "git ls-files: only README.md, app.js, index.html, styles.css, skills-lock.json, .gitignore are project files" is false. `git ls-files | wc -l` = 235; 229 of those are a vendored `.agents/skills/` tree. Critically, that tree contains `.agents/skills/alphafold-database-fetch-and-analyze/scripts/{fetch_structure.py,analyze_plddt.py,analyze_pae.py}` (Apache-2.0, "Copyright 2026 Google LLC", docstring "Analyzes Predicted Aligned Error (PAE) and detects domain boundaries"). Therefore the overall_assessment sentence "I verified this by enumerating every file in the repository and grepping ... the result is zero matches" is wrong as a whole-repo claim: pLDDT- and PAE-parsing code IS present in the repository. The correct, verified scoping is: zero matches across README.md, app.js and index.html, i.e. the web platform performs no inference and parses no AF3 artifact. Note this makes the finding worse, not better -- genuine AlphaFold-DB pLDDT/PAE parsers sit unused in the same repo while the platform synthesises the same quantities from a sine wave. It also does not rescue the AF3 claim: that skill targets the AlphaFold *Database* (AF2 predictions, keyed on a UniProt accession), not AF3 inference, and nothing in app.js/index.html invokes it. (2) "four CDN asset loads" undercounts: index.html loads five subresources (fonts CSS:11, FontAwesome CSS:13, three.js r128:15, OrbitControls:16, Chart.js:18) across four hosts, plus two preconnects.

Correction: None material. text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on AIML-03: The science is correct and the arithmetic reproduces exactly. Using RT = 0.0019872*298.15 = 0.5925 kcal/mol: dG = -18.4 implies Kd = 3.256e-14 M = 0.0326 pM against a stated 0.32 nM, a factor of 9828 (finding says ~9,800). Mean log10 discrepancy across the 25 = 3.471 (finding says 10^3.47). Regressing log10(Kd in M) on dG: slope 0.41130, r = +0.99695, implied RT = 1.0559 kcal/mol, implied T = 531.3 K. All exact. Spearman(rank, pLDDT) = -0.612 and Spearman(rank, CEI) = -0.988, both exact. CEI is genuinely undefined: `grep -rniE 'cei|cognitive enhancement'` across all four files returns only the data field (app.js:125-134), the `<th>CEI Score</th>` at index.html:306, the chart title at index.html:316 and the series label at app.js:1063 -- no formula, no inputs, no units. ipTM/pTM/ranking_score/has_clash/chain_pair grep to zero. The AF3 semantics quoted (per-atom pLDDT; PAE as token x token relative position/orientation error; ipTM as subunit-placement accuracy; ranking_score in [-100,1.5]) I verified verbatim against docs/output.md this session, and Abramson et al. is real (PubMed 38718835, Nature 630(8016):493-500, DOI 10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w). Correction: (1) "The leaderboard is actually sorted by CEI" is not exactly true and should be restated. rho(rank,CEI) = -0.988, not -1: ranks 3 and 4 are inverted (CEI 92.1 at rank 3 sits above CEI 93.8 at rank 4). rho(rank,dG) = +0.964, close behind. So the correct and stronger statement is: the displayed ordering is not reproduced exactly by ANY of the three published columns -- it is unexplained by pLDDT, by dG, and by the undefined CEI. (2) The Bennett et al. characterisation is slightly over-sharpened. I pulled the abstract from PubMed (PMID 37149653, Nat Commun 14:2625, DOI 10.1038/s41467-023-38328-5): the ~10-fold gain comes from using AF2/RoseTTAFold to assess BOTH "the probability that a designed sequence adopts the designed monomer structure" AND "the probability that this structure binds the target as designed". pae_interaction is the decisive interface term, but the filter is a conjunction that includes monomer self-consistency, so "not monomer confidence" should read "monomer confidence alone is insufficient; the interface term is what carries the gain". This does not weaken the finding -- the platform has neither term, since it never predicts a complex. (3) Karelina et al. is real and correctly summarised (PMID 38131311, eLife 12, DOI 10.7554/eLife.89386); the reviewed-preprint id RP89386 is fine, PubMed records e89386.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on AIML-04: I re-implemented the geometry loop from app.js:711-729 and measured consecutive control-point spacing. HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 (36 aa): min 1.21, max 15.77, mean 6.41 -- exact match to the finding. HippoNrf-KeapDecoy-X3 (28 aa): min 0.63, max 16.63, mean 7.90 -- exact match. (HippoTrk-Saponin-X1, 47 aa: 1.91 to 19.08, mean 6.62.) Against a real trans Ca(i)-Ca(i+1) of 3.80 +/- 0.04 A these are physically impossible, as claimed. sed confirms every cited line verbatim: app.js:707 "// REAL FASTA SEQUENCE PARSING & 3D BACKBONE TOPOLOGY GENERATION"; app.js:715 `radius = 6 + (charCode % 5) * 0.8`; app.js:717 the 6-or-4 turn selector keyed on charCode%3, which does fix turn count independent of length so pitch scales with N; app.js:723 the C/P 1.3x scaling; app.js:747-749 the three colour assignments with the literal comments "// Very High (>90)", "// High", "// Low" keyed on residue letter, never on any pLDDT value; app.js:757-761 a fixed 2.2-radius wireframe sphere at (0,0,0) (and app.js:1012-1021, radius 2.5, same origin) identical for every entry. The alpha-helix reference values quoted (2.3 A radius, 1.5 A rise, 3.6 res/turn; beta 3.3-3.4 A rise; cis-Pro ~2.9 A) are standard and correct. Correction: (1) "92.4% of those same residues above 90" is the fraction at >= 90; strictly > 90 (the AlphaFold 'very high' band boundary) is 89.8%. Immaterial to the argument but should be stated as ">= 90" for exactness. (2) One additional defect in the same code that the finding should absorb rather than leave for later: the residue markers are not registered to the residues they are coloured by. app.js:744 positions each sphere at `curve.getPoint(i / seqLength)` while app.js:745 colours it by `sequence[i]`. In three.js r128, CatmullRomCurve3.getPoint(t) maps t to control index (N-1)*t, so the marker for residue i lands at control index i - i/N -- a displacement growing to nearly a full residue at the C-terminus. So even taken on its own terms the panel mislabels which bead is which residue.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on AIML-05: Verified by inspection of the full data block. Every one of the 25 entries in FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA (app.js:138-398) carries exactly one structural input field, `sequence`, and every one of the 10 AF3_CANDIDATES (app.js:125-134) carries exactly one, `fasta`. app.js:142 is verbatim "Ginsenoside Rg1 Dammarane-12,20-diol (C42H72O14) + C-20 Linker" and app.js:144 verbatim "TrkB Ig-like D5 Domain (Asp298, Glu319, Tyr342, Val312, Leu333)", both free text. There is no SMILES field, no CCD code, no ccdCodes list, no bondedAtomPairs, no receptor sequence and no UniProt accession anywhere in the 25-drug or 10-candidate records (the only SMILES strings in the repo are the eight natural-product literals at app.js:10-80, which are never passed to any renderer -- openDrugModal at app.js:648-652 forwards only `drug.sequence`). So the claimed jobs are lone unbound peptides, and ipTM, chain_pair_pae_min, an inter-chain PAE block, a dG and a Kd are all undefined for a monomer. The conclusion is correct and important. Correction: The required_fix contains a technical error that matters because we intend to implement it. It says to carry "the warhead as SMILES or CCD plus the covalent bond specification to the conjugation residue." That is not implementable on the SMILES branch: google-deepmind/alphafold3 docs/input.md, which I fetched this session, states that SMILES ligands "don't support bonds" to other entities, and directs that for bonded ligands you must use a CCD code or the user-provided-CCD format; `bondedAtomPairs` endpoints are (entity id, 1-based residue id, atom name), which SMILES cannot supply because it defines no unique atom names. Rewrite the fix as: warhead as a CCD code or a user-provided CCD block (never bare SMILES) whenever a covalent linkage to the peptide must be modelled; SMILES is acceptable only for a non-covalently docked warhead. Separately, the ground_truth asserts UniProt Q16620 for the TrkB D5 domain; I did not verify that accession in this session, so either check it before issue or drop the accession and say "the receptor's UniProt accession and the exact domain boundaries used".

text: Verdict CONFIRMED on AIML-06: I scanned all 25 modal sequences and all 10 leaderboard FASTAs against ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY. Exactly three drug entries and one leaderboard entry fail, and they are the ones cited: HippoWnt-FzdAgonist-X4 (app.js:173) and AstroZo1-Protect-A3 (app.js:371), both 31 aa with 'B' at 0-based index 18, and CogWnt-Fzd-09 (app.js:130), 40 aa with 'B' at index 18 -- so the index-18 claim is exact in all three. AstroPafr-Block-A4 (app.js:381) is `sequence: "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate"`, 37 characters containing 19 distinct non-residue characters ('-', digits 1/4/7, and lowercase a,d,e,g,h,i,j,k,n,o,p,r,s,t,u). It is passed unvalidated through app.js:648-652 into all three renderers; my reimplementation of the generator on that string produces a complete 37-point curve with mean 94.09, and app.js:384 prints "AF3 pLDDT = 92.4 / 100" for it. There is no validation function and no error path anywhere in app.js. The reasoning that a real pipeline would have failed loudly is sound, and the Copy-FASTA consequence follows. Correction: One narrow precision point on the ground_truth. docs/input.md (fetched this session) says only that protein sequences use "the 1-letter standard amino acid codes"; it does not enumerate the alphabet and says nothing about X/UNK, B, Z or J. So the claim "X (UNK) is handled specially and is not a substitute" is not documented and should be dropped or hedged. The defensible statement is: B/Z/J are alignment-format ambiguity codes, are outside the documented standard 20-letter set, and non-standard residues are expressed instead through the separate `modifications` field with a CCD `ptmType` and 1-based `ptmPosition` -- which I did verify verbatim.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED on AIML-07: I verified the legal claims against primary sources this session rather than taking them on faith. WEIGHTS_TERMS_OF_USE.md from google-deepmind/alphafold3: access limited to "non-commercial organizations (i.e., universities, non-profit organizations and research institutes, educational, journalism and government bodies)"; "You must not use nor allow others to use: AlphaFold 3 model parameters or output in connection with any commercial activities, including research on behalf of commercial organizations"; "You must not publish or share AlphaFold 3 model parameters, except sharing these within your organization"; and a prohibition on using AF3 output to train competing structure predictors. The repo license via the GitHub API is Apache-2.0 for code, exactly as stated. The AlphaFold Server Prohibited Use Policy language about not using the service or its outputs "in connection with any automated system that predicts the binding or interaction of the protein with ligands or peptides, including, but not limited to, Glide or AutoDock" is confirmed (alphafoldserver.com/prohibited-use), and the finding correctly scopes it to the Server rather than the open-source release. The 10-then-20 jobs/day quota is confirmed. All four recommended alternatives check out via the GitHub API: jwohlwend/boltz MIT (repo states "MIT License, and can be freely used for both academic and commercial purposes"; Boltz-2 emits `affinity_pred_value` as "log10(IC50), derived from an IC50 measured in uM" plus `affinity_probability_binary`; preprint DOIs 10.1101/2024.11.19.624167 and 10.1101/2025.06.14.659707 are the ones the repo lists), chaidiscovery/chai-lab Apache-2.0 with the verbatim statement "Chai-1 is released under an Apache 2.0 License (both code and model weights), which means it can be used for both academic and commerical purposes, including for drug discovery", bytedance/Protenix Apache-2.0, and aqlaboratory/openfold-3 Apache-2.0, "A fully open source biomolecular structure prediction model based on AlphaFold3". The branding claims are verbatim in the files: README.md:3 shields.io badge "AlphaFold3-DeepMind_Server" with logo=google, index.html:30 "DeepMind Structural Pharmacology & AlphaFold3 De Novo Platform", index.html:410 "Generated with AlphaFold3 3D Structural Modeling". Correction: Three sub-claims I could not verify and which should be softened or dropped rather than issued as fact. (1) "exposes no API" and "supports only a restricted CCD-based ligand set rather than arbitrary SMILES" for AlphaFold Server: alphafoldserver.com/faq returned no extractable body to me this session, and the open-source AF3 does accept SMILES, so this contrast is unverified as stated -- drop it, it carries no weight in the finding. (2) "Protenix reports outperforming AlphaFold3 across benchmark sets at matched training-data cutoff, model scale, and inference budget" -- not verified; state it as the authors' claim or omit. (3) "OpenFold3 ... ships full training data and a trainable framework" -- not verified; the repo description confirms only that it is a fully open-source AF3-class model under Apache-2.0. Also note for the fix: renaming the local directory /Users/.../DeepMind_Bio is cosmetic and does not travel with the repository; the substantive items are the badge, the subtitle and the footer.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED on AIML-08: Verified by reading the code path rather than trusting the description. initModal3DCanvas clears the container with `container.innerHTML = ''` (app.js:678), constructs a new THREE.WebGLRenderer on every open (app.js:688) and appends its canvas (app.js:691); nothing calls dispose(), forceContextLoss(), or traverses the scene disposing geometries and materials. The animation closure at app.js:763-772 guards on `if (!modalThreeRenderer) return;` (app.js:764) -- and modalThreeRenderer is a module-scope binding declared at app.js:410 that the next open reassigns, so the stale closure sees a truthy value, does not exit, mutates `modalThreeMeshGroup` (also module-scope, now the new group) at app.js:767-768 and calls render on the current renderer/scene/camera at app.js:770. After k opens, k loops each add 0.006 rad/frame to the same group and each issue a render of the same scene. closeDrugModal (app.js:655-658) only removes a CSS class; it cancels no rAF and disposes nothing. Chrome's per-page live-WebGL-context cap of ~16 is the correct order of magnitude, and 25 drug cards is more than 16, so the failure is reachable by ordinary use. Severity MINOR is right -- it is a genuine but non-scientific defect, and the finding is honest that it would survive a correct viewer rewrite. Correction: None.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: THE STRONGEST AVAILABLE PROOF OF FABRICATION WAS MISSED: identical sequences carry different 'AF3' numbers. Four sequences appear twice in the 25-drug set with contradictory metrics -- KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG is both HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 (app.js:153, dG -16.2, Kd 2.1 nM, pLDDT 94.8) and BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1 (app.js:247, dG -17.5, Kd 0.65 nM, pLDDT 94.3); SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGCDERACPRCHGFWREVC is both PfcACh-PAM-P1 (app.js:195, pLDDT 93.2) and MicroTlr4-Antagonist-M3 (app.js:319, pLDDT 92.8); CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH is X4 (app.js:173, 95.1) and A3 (app.js:371, 93.8); VRACPTGKCEGLRGYTCRCEPGWKGPDCRERACPDCH is P2 (app.js:205, 95.8) and A2 (app.js:361, 94.1). Seven more collisions exist between drug sequences and leaderboard FASTAs with different pLDDT (e.g. X2 == CogAChE-PAS-02, 94.8 vs 92.8; P1 == CognACh-Mod-06, 93.2 vs 90.7). A deterministic model given identical input cannot return different confidences. This needs no formula reverse-engineering, no arithmetic and no external ground truth -- it is visible by sorting the array. Worse, the same peptide is claimed to bind unrelated receptors (alpha7 nAChR ECD vs TLR4/MD-2; FZD8 CRD vs ZO-1/occludin; TrkB D5 vs the EAAT2 transporter), which is a target-assignment fabrication independent of the numbers. And because the generators are deterministic, those four card pairs render byte-identical pLDDT curves, PAE heatmaps and 3D models -- 8 of the 25 modals are visually indistinguishable in pairs.

tags: Machine learning for protein structure prediction (AlphaFold-class models): model outputs, confidence calibration, de novo binder design evaluation, and inference infrastructure
text: Missed by the primary reviewer: AF3 IS NOT A DESIGN MODEL -- the headline claim is a category error, not merely unimplemented. README.md:22 and README.md:45 say the 25 therapeutics were 'designed via AlphaFold3' and 'AlphaFold3-optimized binding loop peptides'; index.html:290 labels the field 'FASTA Sequence (AlphaFold3 Design)'. AF3 is a structure predictor: it consumes a sequence and emits coordinates and confidences. It has no generative sequence head and cannot propose, optimise or mutate a binder. De novo binder design requires a separate generative stack (RFdiffusion / ProteinMPNN / BindCraft / hallucination), none of which is named anywhere. The reviewer argues at length that AF3 was never RUN; the deeper point is that even a perfect AF3 run could not have produced these sequences. Relatedly, 'de novo' is false on its own terms: the peptides are concatenations of known natural motifs the review itself identifies as authentic (KLVFFAED = Abeta16-23, DEETGE = the Nrf2 Neh2 ETGE motif, GRPRTTSFAESC = the GSK-3beta Ser9 substrate motif, GGGGS spacers). Copied motifs joined by linkers are a fusion construct, not a de novo design.

tags: Machine learning for protein structure prediction (AlphaFold-class models): model outputs, confidence calibration, de novo binder design evaluation, and inference infrastructure
text: Missed by the primary reviewer: ZERO REPRODUCIBILITY METADATA, which is the first thing a Nature Methods reviewer checks. There is no seed, no sample index, no model version, no run date, no software version and no error bar anywhere in the repository (`grep -niE 'seed|model_version|sample|version'` over app.js and README.md returns only the unrelated word 'seeding' in two mechanism strings). AF3 by default runs multiple seeds x multiple diffusion samples and ranks across them via ranking_scores.csv; pLDDT varies materially between samples. Quoting 35 pLDDT values to 0.1 with no seed, no sample count and no spread is by itself grounds for rejection even if a model had been run, and it should be a named requirement of the AIML-01 fix: persist seed, sample, model version and the per-sample spread alongside every number surfaced.

tags: Machine learning for protein structure prediction (AlphaFold-class models): model outputs, confidence calibration, de novo binder design evaluation, and inference infrastructure
text: Missed by the primary reviewer: NO CALIBRATION, NO CONTROLS, AND AN IMPLIED 100% HIT RATE. The discipline here is 'confidence calibration' and the review never asks the calibration question. There is no held-out set, no reliability diagram, no negative control, no scrambled-sequence or shuffled-linker baseline, no decoy targets, and no experimental validation path. All 25 candidates are reported as successes with sub-10 nM Kd and 15 of 25 below 2 nM. Against the literature baseline the review itself cites (Bennett et al. 2023, PMID 37149653), AF-filtered de novo binder campaigns run at single-digit percent experimental success. A pipeline reporting 25/25 is reporting an impossibility, and that is checkable without reading a line of code -- it should be its own finding, because it is the one a funder or collaborator can evaluate.

tags: Machine learning for protein structure prediction (AlphaFold-class models): model outputs, confidence calibration, de novo binder design evaluation, and inference infrastructure
text: Missed by the primary reviewer: THE FABRICATION POINTS THE WRONG WAY FOR THIS INPUT CLASS, which is the specifically ML observation. Short de novo peptides have essentially no MSA depth; AF2/AF3-class models give isolated 28-47mer peptides with no receptor and no homologs LOW and poorly calibrated pLDDT, frequently 40-70 with wide seed-to-seed variance, not the 89.0-99.0 band the generator produces. So a domain reader is not merely seeing invented numbers, they are seeing numbers whose central tendency is inverted relative to what this exact input class produces. The same inversion applies at the linkers (which the review does catch) and at the termini. Any relabelling fix should say so explicitly, because 'placeholder data' understates it -- the placeholder is anti-correlated with reality.

tags: Machine learning for protein structure prediction (AlphaFold-class models): model outputs, confidence calibration, de novo binder design evaluation, and inference infrastructure
text: Missed by the primary reviewer: THE PAE PANEL IS BROKEN AS A VISUALISATION INDEPENDENT OF ITS CONTENTS. index.html:399 sizes the canvas 540x220 while app.js:845-846 compute cellW = width/gridSize and cellH = height/gridSize, so a square token x token matrix is drawn stretched 2.45:1 horizontally for every single drug (12.00 x 4.89 px cells at gridSize 45). A PAE matrix that is not square is unreadable as a PAE matrix -- the diagonal is not a diagonal. On top of that, app.js:853-862 encode error with a three-step hard-switched hue AND an alpha ramp of 1 - error/35, so high-error cells fade to the page background: the encoding is non-monotonic in perceived lightness, has no colourbar, and has no axis ticks or chain dividers. Even after a real confidences.json is wired in, this renderer would misdisplay it. The AIML-02 fix should require a square canvas, a monotonic sequential colormap, a labelled colourbar in Angstroms, and chain-boundary rules.

tags: Machine learning for protein structure prediction (AlphaFold-class models): model outputs, confidence calibration, de novo binder design evaluation, and inference infrastructure
text: Missed by the primary reviewer: THE pLDDT CHART AXIS GUARANTEES A FLAT LINE. app.js:824-825 pin the y-axis to [50, 100] while the data are confined to [89.0, 99.0]. Every one of the 25 curves therefore renders as a nearly flat trace pressed against the ceiling, occupying the top fifth of the plot, under a four-band legend (index.html:388-391) whose lower two bands can never be reached. The visual message 'uniformly maximal confidence, no variation worth reading' is manufactured by the axis choice as much as by the generator, and the fix list should say to derive the axis from the data or use the standard 0-100 with band shading.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: NO PROVENANCE OR AUDIT TRAIL AS A GENERAL REQUIREMENT. The review frames the problem correctly as a provenance failure but stops at deletion and relabelling. The structural fix is a provenance contract: every displayed number should carry the artifact path it was read from, the model and version that produced it, and the run timestamp, and the UI should be incapable of displaying a metric that has no such backing. Without that, the same class of defect reappears the first time someone hand-edits a value. This should be stated as an acceptance criterion for the AIML-01 remediation, not left implicit.
